facts.statement: The genus Pterodactylus was originally placed under the authority of Bonaparte in 1838.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Bonaparte, 1838

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Ornithocephalus antiquus.
facts.quote: type_species: Ornithocephalus antiquus

facts.statement: The species P. antiquus was named by Sömmerring in 1812.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. antiquus (Sömmerring, 1812)

facts.statement: The name Pterodactylus means 'winged finger' and it is a genus of extinct pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus (from winged finger) is a genus of extinct pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus antiquus is thought to be the only species in the genus and was the first pterosaur identified as a flying reptile.
facts.quote: It is thought to contain only a single species, Pterodactylus antiquus, which was the first pterosaur to be named and identified as a flying reptile and one of the first prehistoric reptiles ever to be discovered.

facts.statement: Fossils of Pterodactylus are primarily found in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dating from the Late Jurassic Tithonian stage between 150.8 and 148.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of Pterodactylus have primarily been found in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, which dates from the Late Jurassic period (Tithonian stage), about 150.8 to 148.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus was a generalist carnivore that likely ate a variety of invertebrates and vertebrates.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus was a generalist carnivore that probably fed on a variety of invertebrates and vertebrates.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus was a small pterosaur that lived earlier than the Late Cretaceous genera Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus was a small pterosaur compared to other famous genera such as Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus, and it also lived earlier, during the Late Jurassic period, while both Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus lived during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The first Pterodactylus specimen was described by Cosimo Alessandro Collini in 1784 from fossils found in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria.
facts.quote: The first Pterodactylus specimen was described by the Italian scientist Cosimo Alessandro Collini in 1784, based on a fossil skeleton that had been unearthed from the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria.

facts.statement: Collini speculated the animal might be a sea creature because he believed ocean depths were more likely to hold unknown animals.
facts.quote: He speculated that it may have been a sea creature, not for any anatomical reason, but because he thought the ocean depths were more likely to have housed unknown types of animals.

facts.statement: The idea that pterosaurs were aquatic persisted until 1830, when Johann Georg Wagler illustrated Pterodactylus using its wings as flippers.
facts.quote: The idea that pterosaurs were aquatic animals persisted among a minority of scientists as late as 1830, when the German zoologist Johann Georg Wagler published a text on "amphibians" which included an illustration of Pterodactylus using its wings as flippers.

facts.statement: Georges Cuvier first published the idea that the animal was a reptile with wing membranes in December 1800.
facts.quote: Cuvier became the first to publish these ideas in December 1800 in a very short description.

facts.statement: Cuvier named the animal Petro-Dactyle in 1809, a typo later corrected to Ptéro-Dactyle.
facts.quote: In 1809 Cuvier published a somewhat longer description, in which he named the animal Petro-Dactyle, this was a typographical error however, and was later corrected by him to Ptéro-Dactyle.

facts.statement: Cuvier refuted the hypothesis by Johann Friedrich Blumenbach that the animal was a shore bird.
facts.quote: He also refuted a hypothesis by Johann Friedrich Blumenbach that it would have been a shore bird.

facts.statement: A second specimen of Pterodactylus was discovered in 1817 from Solnhofen.
facts.quote: It was not until 1817 that a second specimen of Pterodactylus came to light, again from Solnhofen.

facts.statement: The adult Pterodactylus antiquus had an estimated wingspan of about 1.04 meters based on an isolated skull.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus antiquus was a relatively small pterosaur, with an estimated adult wingspan of about 1.04 m, based on the only known adult specimen, which is represented by an isolated skull.

facts.statement: Adult Pterodactylus skulls were long and thin, containing approximately 90 narrow and conical teeth.
facts.quote: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin, with about 90 narrow and conical teeth.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus is distinguished by having straight skulls and jaws, unlike the upwardly curved jaws of related ctenochasmatids.
facts.quote: Another autapomorphy that Pterodactylus has is that the skull and jaws were straight, which are unlike the upwardly curved jaws seen in the related ctenochasmatids.

facts.statement: In adults, the soft tissue crest of Pterodactylus extended from the back edge of the antorbital fenestra to the back of the skull.
facts.quote: In adult Pterodactylus, this crest extended between the back edge of the antorbital fenestra and the back of the skull.

facts.statement: Solid crests were found only on large, fully adult Pterodactylus, suggesting the crest was a display structure that developed with maturity.
facts.quote: Solid crests have only been found on large, fully adult specimens of Pterodactylus, indicating that this was a display structure that became larger and more well developed as individuals reached maturity.

facts.statement: Some specimens preserved evidence of a soft tissue extension called an "occipital lappet" extending from the back of the skull.
facts.quote: Several specimens previously referred to P. antiquus preserved evidence of the soft tissue extensions of these crests, including an "occipital lappet", a flexible, tab-like structure extending from the back of the skull.

facts.statement: Youngest immature P. antiquus specimens had as few as 15 teeth with relatively broad bases.
facts.quote: The youngest immature specimens of Pterodactylus antiquus (alternately interpreted as young specimens of the distinct species P. kochi) have a small number of teeth, as few as 15 in some, and the teeth have a relatively broad base.

facts.statement: Other P. antiquus specimens had narrower and more numerous teeth, up to 90 in some cases.
facts.quote: The teeth of other P. antiquus specimens are both narrower and more numerous (up to 90 teeth are present in several specimens).

facts.statement: A third year class of P. antiquus specimens, including some large ones once assigned to P. kochi, all show signs of immaturity.
facts.quote: A third year class is represented by specimens of the "traditional" P. antiquus, as well as a few isolated, large specimens once assigned to P. kochi that overlap P. antiquus in size. However, all specimens in this third year class also show sign of immaturity.

facts.statement: Distinct year classes in P. antiquus fossils suggest the species bred seasonally and grew consistently throughout its life.
facts.quote: The distinct year classes of Pterodactylus antiquus specimens show that this species, like the contemporary Rhamphorhynchus muensteri, likely bred seasonally and grew consistently during its lifetime.

facts.statement: The smallest size class of P. antiquus likely consisted of individuals less than one year old that had just begun to fly.
facts.quote: The smallest size class probably consisted of individuals that had just begun to fly and were less than one year old.

facts.statement: The second year class of P. antiquus represented individuals one to two years old, while the rare third year class included specimens over two years old.
facts.quote: The second year class represents individuals one to two years old, and the rare third year class is composed of specimens over two years old.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest P. antiquus may have been diurnal.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Pterodactylus antiquus and modern birds and reptiles suggest that it may have been diurnal.

facts.statement: The Solnhofen Limestone is a diverse fossil site containing detailed imprints of soft-bodied organisms like jellyfishes.
facts.quote: The Solnhofen Limestone is a diverse Lagerstätte that contains a wide range of different creatures, including highly detailed fossilized imprints of soft bodied organisms such as jellyfishes.

facts.statement: In 1846, Hermann von Meyer described the species Pterodactylus gemmingi, a name honoring fossil collector Carl Eming von Gemming.
facts.quote: In 1846, von Meyer created the new species Pterodactylus gemmingi based on long-tailed remains; the specific name honors the fossil collector Carl Eming von Gemming.

facts.statement: Starting in 1846, British paleontologists James Scott Bowerbank and Sir Richard Owen discovered numerous pterosaur specimens near Burham in Kent, England.
facts.quote: Beginning in 1846, many pterosaur specimens were found near the village of Burham in Kent, England by British paleontologists James Scott Bowerbank and Sir Richard Owen.

facts.statement: In 1851, Sir Richard Owen assigned newly found English specimens to the species Pterodactylus compressirostris.
facts.quote: In 1851, Owen named and described new pterosaur specimens that have been found yet again in England. He assigned these specimens to a new species called Pterodactylus compressirostris.

facts.statement: In 1859, Sir Richard Owen named Pterodactylus segwickii after British geologist Adam Sedgwick based on a snout fragment from the Cambridge Greensand.
facts.quote: In 1859, Owen had found remains the front part of a snout in the Cambridge Greensand, and assigned it into the species Pterodactylus segwickii; in honor of Adam Sedgwick, a British geologist.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Samuel Wendell Williston discovered the first skull of Pterodactylus and determined that the animal was toothless.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Samuel Wendell Williston unearthed the first skull of the pterosaur, and found that the animal was toothless

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh described several toothless pterosaur specimens in 1871.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh in 1871 for example, described several toothless pterosaur specimens

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope assigned two North American pterosaur specimens to the species Ornithochirus umbrosus and Ornithochirus harpyia.
facts.quote: Edward Drinker Cope also found various pterosaur specimens in North America, he assigned these to two new species known as Ornithochirus umbrosus and Ornithochirus harpyia

facts.statement: In 1875, Edward Drinker Cope reassigned the species to Pterodactylus umbrosus and Pterodactylus harpyia.
facts.quote: In 1875 however, Cope reassigned the species O. umbrosus and O. harpyia into Pterodactylus umbrosus and Pterodactylus harpyia

facts.statement: Revisions by Peter Wellnhofer in the 1980s reduced the number of recognized Pterodactylus species to about six.
facts.quote: Later, in the 1980s, subsequent revisions by Peter Wellnhofer had reduced the number of recognized species to about half a dozen

facts.statement: Studies found that Pterodactylus elegans was actually an immature individual of the genus Ctenochasma.
facts.quote: P. elegans, for example, was found by numerous studies to be an immature Ctenochasma

facts.statement: In 2013, Christopher Bennett assigned Pterodactylus micronyx to the genus Aurorazhdarcho.
facts.quote: After additional research in 2013, Bennett assigned it to the genus Aurorazhdarcho

facts.statement: Pterodactylus longicollum was eventually designated as the type species of the separate genus Ardeadactylus.
facts.quote: "P." longicollum was eventually made the type species of a separate genus Ardeadactylus

facts.statement: In 1996, Christopher Bennett suggested that differences between Pterodactylus kochi and P. antiquus were due to age differences, making them the same species.
facts.quote: In 1996, Bennett suggested that the differences between specimens of P. kochi and P. antiquus could be explained by differences in age

facts.statement: In 2017, Christopher Bennett argued that the differences identified by Vidovic and Martill were not sufficient to justify separating them into three distinct species.
facts.quote: In 2017, Bennett challenged this hypothesis, he claimed that while Vidovic and Martill had identified real differences between these three groups of specimens, they had not provided any rationale that the differences were enough to distinguish them as species

facts.statement: By the early 21st century, Pterodactylus antiquus and P. kochi were the only well-known and well-supported species remaining.
facts.quote: The only well-known and well-supported species left by the first decades of the 21st century were P. antiquus and P. kochi

facts.statement: Vidovic and Martill named the new genus Aerodactylus for the species P. scolopaciceps.
facts.quote: They named the new genus Aerodactylus for P. scolopaciceps as well

facts.statement: American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope discovered various pterosaur specimens in North America in 1872.
facts.quote: In 1872, American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope also found various pterosaur specimens in North America

facts.statement: By the 1990s, it was understood that some of the remaining Pterodactylus species were also based on immature individuals.
facts.quote: By the 1990s it was understood that this was even true for part of the remaining species

facts.statement: Over its 200-year history, Pterodactylus has undergone numerous classification changes, resulting in many synonyms.
facts.quote: During its over-200-year history, the various species of Pterodactylus have gone through a number of changes in classification and thus have acquired a large number of synonyms

facts.statement: Several species assigned to Pterodactylus are considered nomina dubia because they are based on poor remains that are difficult to classify.
facts.quote: Additionally, a number of species assigned to Pterodactylus are based on poor remains that have proven difficult to assign to one species or another and are therefore considered nomina dubia

facts.statement: The informal term "pterodactyl" is often mistakenly used to refer to any pterosaur, but specifically applies to Pterodactylus and the unrelated Pteranodon.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus is popularly known for its elongated head crest and large wings.
facts.quote: The popular aspect of Pterodactylus consists of an elongated head crest, and potentially large wings.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pterodactylus possessed a bony crest or a soft-tissue crest, with some studies suggesting it may lack a bony cranial crest entirely.
facts.quote: Studies of Pterodactylus, however, conclude that it may even lack a bony cranial crest, though several analysis have proven that Pterodactylus may in fact have a crest made up of soft tissue instead of bone.

facts.statement: The flying monsters ridden by the Nazgûl in J.R.R. Tolkien's legendarium were described as looking similarly built to Pterodactylus.
facts.quote: In this novel, the Nazgûl, introduced as the Black Riders, are nine characters who rode flying monsters that looked similarly built to Pterodactylus.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus was the first pterosaur to be named and identified as a flying reptile.
facts.quote: Fue el primero en ser nombrado e identificado como un reptil volador.

facts.statement: Fossils of Pterodactylus are primarily found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dating to the late Jurassic (early Tithonian) between 150.8 and 148.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles han sido hallados primordialmente en la Caliza de Solnhofen de Baviera, Alemania, que data de finales del período Jurásico (principios del Titoniense), hace entre 150.8-148.5 millones de años

facts.statement: Pterodactylus was a carnivore that likely hunted fish and other small animals.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro y probablemente cazaba peces y otros animales pequeños.

facts.statement: Like all pterosaurs, Pterodactylus wings were formed by a muscle and skin membrane extending from its elongated fourth finger to its hind limbs.
facts.quote: Como todos los pterosaurios, las alas de Pterodactylus estaban formadas por una membrana de músculo y piel que se extendía desde su alargado cuarto dedo hasta sus miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus was a relatively small pterosaur with an estimated adult wingspan of 1.5 meters for P. antiquus.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus era un pterosaurio relativamente pequeño, con una envergadura adulta estimada en 1.5 metros para P. antiquus.

facts.statement: Adult Pterodactylus skulls were long and narrow, featuring nearly 90 large conical teeth.
facts.quote: Los cráneos de los Pterodactylus adultos eran largos y estrechos con cerca de 90 grandes dientes cónicos.

facts.statement: Pterodactylus had a long neck covered in long, bristle-like pycnofibers.
facts.quote: El cuello era largo, y cubierto de largas picnofibras parecidas a cerdas.

facts.statement: Crests were only found in fully developed adult specimens, indicating they were display structures that developed upon reaching maturity.
facts.quote: Las crestas sólo se han hallado en los especímenes mayores y completamente desarrollados de Pterodactylus, indicando que esta era una estructura de exhibición y sólo se desarrollaba cuando los individuos alcanzaban la madurez.

facts.statement: In specimen BMMS 7, the bony crest measured 47.5 millimeters in length (about 24% of the estimated skull length) and had a maximum height of 0.9 millimeters above the orbit.
facts.quote: en BMMS 7 es de 47.5 milímetros de largo (más o menos el 24% de la longitud estimada de ese cráneo) y una altura máxima de 0.9 milímetros sobre la órbita.

facts.statement: Age groups in Pterodactylus antiquus suggest the species likely reproduced seasonally and grew consistently throughout its life, similar to its contemporary Rhamphorhynchus muensteri.
facts.quote: Los distintos grupos por edad de los especímenes de Pterodactylus antiquus muestran que esta especie, como su contemporáneo Rhamphorhynchus muensteri, probablemente se reproducían estacionalmente y crecían de modo consistente durante su vida.

facts.statement: The smallest size class likely consisted of individuals who had just begun to fly and were less than one year old.
facts.quote: La clase de menor tamaño probablemente consistía de individuos que apenas habían empezado a volar y eran de menos de un año de edad.

facts.statement: The second age group represented individuals one to two years old, while the rare third group consisted of specimens older than two years.
facts.quote: El segundo grupo por edad representa individuos de uno a dos años de edad, y el menos común tercer grupo por edad se compone de especímenes de más de dos años de edad.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral ring patterns suggest Pterodactylus antiquus may have been diurnal.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones hechas entre los anillos escleróticos de Pterodactylus antiquus y las aves y reptiles modernos sugieren que pueden haber sido diurnos.

facts.statement: This suggests an ecological niche division from contemporary pterosaurs inferred to be nocturnal, such as Ctenochasma and Rhamphorhynchus.
facts.quote: Esto puede indicar una división de nichos ecológicos con pterosaurios contemporáneos de los que se infiere que eran nocturnos, como Ctenochasma y Rhamphorhynchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether fully adult Pterodactylus specimens are unknown or were mistakenly classified as other genera.
facts.quote: Los especímenes de Pterodactylus totalmente adultos aún son desconocidos, o pueden haber sido clasificados erróneamente como otro género.

facts.statement: The first specimen of Pterodactylus was described by Italian scientist Cosimo Alessandro Collini in 1784 based on a fossil skeleton unearthed from the Solnhofen Limestone of Bavaria.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen de Pterodactylus fue descrito por el científico italiano Cosimo Alessandro Collini en 1784, basándose en un esqueleto fósil desenterrado de la Caliza de Solnhofen de Baviera.

facts.statement: The animal now known as Pterodactylus was the first pterosaur to be identified.
facts.quote: El animal ahora conocido como Pterodactylus fue el primer pterosaurio en ser identificado.

facts.statement: Collini did not conclude that the animal was a flying creature.
facts.quote: Collini, sin embargo, no concluyó que se trataba de un animal volador.

facts.statement: Collini speculated that the animal might have been a marine creature, not for anatomical reasons, but because he believed ocean depths were a more likely home for unknown animal types.
facts.quote: Él especuló que pudo haber sido una criatura marina, no por razones anatómicas, sino porque él pensaba que las profundidades de los océanos eran un hogar más probable para los tipos de animales desconocidos.

facts.statement: Franco-German scientist Johann Hermann was the first to establish that Pterodactylus used its elongated fourth finger to support a wing membrane.
facts.quote: Fue el científico franco-alemán Johann Hermann el primero en establecer que Pterodactylus usaba su alargado cuarto dedo para sujetar una membrana alar.

facts.statement: Hermann sent Cuvier a letter containing his own interpretation of the specimen, which he believed to be a mammal, including the first life reconstruction of a pterosaur.
facts.quote: Hermann envió a Cuvier una carta conteniendo su propia interpretación del espécimen (aunque él no lo había examinado personalmente), el cual él creía que era un mamífero, incluyendo la primera recreación en vida de un pterosaurio.

facts.statement: Hermann reconstructed the animal with wing membranes extending from the elongated fourth finger to the ankle and a coat of hair, although no traces of membranes or hair had been found on this specimen.
facts.quote: Hermann reconstruyó al animal con membranas alares extendiéndose desde el alargado cuarto dedo hasta el tobillo y una cubierta de pelo (en este espécimen no se había descubierto ningún rastro de membranas ni de pelo).

facts.statement: Cuvier agreed with Hermann's interpretation and, at Hermann's suggestion, became the first to publish these ideas in a very brief description in December 1800.
facts.quote: Cuvier estuvo de acuerdo con su interpretación, y por sugerencia de Hermann, Cuvier se convirtió en el primero en publicar estas ideas en diciembre de 1800 en una muy breve descripción.

facts.statement: Cuvier reiterated that "[It is impossible to doubt that the long finger served to support a membrane that, with the elongation of the anterior limb of this animal, formed a good wing]."
facts.quote: Cuvier recalcó que, "[No es posible dudar de que el largo dedo servía para soportar una membrana que, con el alargamiento de la extremidad anterior de este animal, formaba una buena ala]."

facts.statement: However, contrary to Hermann, Cuvier was convinced that the animal was a reptile.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, de modo contrario a Hermann, Cuvier estaba convencido de que el animal era un reptil.

facts.statement: In 1809 Cuvier published a somewhat longer description, naming the animal, and also refuting Johann Friedrich Blumenbach's hypothesis that it might have been a coastal bird.
facts.quote: En 1809 Cuvier publicó una descripción algo más larga, nombrando el animal, y también refutando la hipótesis de Johann Friedrich Blumenbach de que pudo haber sido un ave costera.

facts.statement: It was not until 1817 that a second specimen of Pterodactylus came to light, again from Solnhofen.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 1817 que salió a la luz un segundo espécimen de Pterodactylus, de nuevo de Solnhofen.

facts.statement: This diminutive specimen was described that year by von Soemmerring as Ornithocephalus brevirostris (due to its short snout, which is now known to be a juvenile trait), and provided a skeleton reconstruction, the first published for any pterosaur.
facts.quote: Este diminuto ejemplar fue ese año descrito por von Soemmerring como Ornithocephalus brevirostris (debido a su corto hocico, que ahora se sabe que es un rasgo juvenil), y proporcionó una reconstrucción del esqueleto, la primera publicada para cualquier pterosaurio.

facts.statement: However, this reconstruction was quite incorrect, as von Soemmerring confused the long metacarpals with forearm bones, the forearm with the humerus, the upper arm with the sternum, and this sternum in turn with the scapula.
facts.quote: Sin embargo esta era bastante incorrecta, ya que von Soemmerring confundió los largos metacarpos con los huesos del antebrazo, el antebrazo con el húmero, la parte superior del brazo con el esternón y este esternón a su vez con el omóplato.
